title: The Association Between Parental Chronic Physical Illness and Adolescent Functional Somatic Symptoms
abstract: ABSTRACT Parental chronic physical illness is a significant yet underrecognized psychosocial stressor with measurable consequences for adolescent health. This narrative review synthesized 54 quantitative, qualitative, and systematic studies drawn from a search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and PsycINFO to examine how parental illness contributes to Functional Somatic Symptoms (FSS) in adolescents. Drawing on the Biopsychosocial Model, Family Stress Theory, and Stress‐Coping frameworks, we identify maladaptive stress‐appraisal and emotional parentification as principal mediators, moderated by adolescent female sex and parental illness severity. Mechanism‐targeted interventions—particularly cognitive‐behavioural therapy and SPACE‐adapted systemic approaches—demonstrate promising outcomes. Clinically, findings support proactive biopsychosocial screening within paediatric primary care. At the policy level, integration models such as the UK's ‘Think Family’ mandate and co‐located Whole‐Family Health Clinics within adult chronic care settings are proposed to interrupt intergenerational health transmission.
